instructions: 1. Introduce the four classical elements: Earth, Air, Fire, and Water. 2. Provide a bin of various LEGO bricks. 3. Ask students to build a representation of each element based on their own understanding. 4. Have students explain why their specific colors and shapes represent that element. 5. Compare different constructions to see how meaning is built individually.

title: Crayon Playdough : 5 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description: Crayon Playdough: Crayon Playdough recipe is very simple to make. You can make different colors of playdough using different shades of crayons. It gives bold color to dough. Try it out for your preschooler, they will love it for sure.
what you'll need: Crayons, flour, salt, water, vegetable oil, cream of tartar
instructions: 1. Grate or chop crayons into small bits. 2. Mix flour, salt, and cream of tartar in a pot. 3. Add water, oil, and the crayon bits. 4. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until a ball forms. 5. The heat melts the crayons into the dough, creating vibrant, bold colors.

title: Rainbow in a Bottle : 6 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description:
Rainbow in a Bottle: This "Rainbow in a Bottle" is a layered solution using different densities of salt water. The materials are super cheap and the end result is impressive.
This project is something I do with my 7th-grade students in my science class. You can find the…
what you'll need: Glass bottle, water, sugar (or salt), food coloring
instructions: 1. Prepare four cups of water with different colors. 2. Add different amounts of sugar/salt to each (e.g., 1 tbsp in red, 2 in yellow, 3 in green, 4 in blue). 3. Stir until dissolved. 4. Carefully layer the liquids in a bottle starting with the densest (most sugar) at the bottom. 5. Use a dropper to slowly add layers to prevent mixing.

title: Large Toy Beads : 10 Steps (with Pictures) - Instructables
description: Large Toy Beads: My daughter got lacing beads as a gift that consisted of square and various round beads she could lace onto a string for fun and hand-eye coordination practice. I thought it would be fun to supplement her set with some other shapes and letters. For …
what you'll need: Wood scraps or thick cardboard, drill, paint, string
instructions: 1. Cut wood or cardboard into various shapes (squares, circles, letters). 2. Drill a hole through the center of each piece. 3. Sand the edges until smooth. 4. Paint the beads in bright colors. 5. Use a thick string or shoelace for the child to practice lacing and pattern making.

title: pressing flowers
what you'll need: Fresh flowers, heavy books, paper towels
instructions: 1. Collect fresh flowers or leaves. 2. Place them between two layers of paper towels. 3. Insert the "sandwich" into the middle of a heavy book. 4. Stack more books on top for weight. 5. Leave for 1-2 weeks until completely dry and flat.

title: raincloud decoration
what you'll need: Cardboard, cotton wool, blue yarn/string, glue
instructions: 1. Cut a cloud shape out of cardboard. 2. Glue pulled-apart cotton wool all over the cloud. 3. Cut several lengths of blue yarn to represent rain. 4. Attach the yarn to the bottom of the cloud. 5. Hang the cloud and watch the "raindrops" dangle.

title: straw oboe
instructions: 1. Flatten about 1 inch of one end of the straw. 2. Cut two small triangles off the corners of the flattened end to create a "V" shape (the reed). 3. Put the V-end in your mouth and blow hard. 4. Trim the straw to see how a shorter length creates a higher pitch. 5. Experiment with blowing pressure to change the sound.

title: toothbrush splatter painting
instructions: 1. Dip an old toothbrush into slightly watered-down paint. 2. Hold the brush over a piece of paper. 3. Run your thumb across the bristles to "flick" the paint. 4. Repeat with different colors to create a starry or textured effect. 5. Use stencils on the paper before spraying for a "negative" image.

title: paper fidgit toy
instructions: 1. Start with a square piece of paper. 2. Follow a series of "valley" and "mountain" folds to create an origami-style structure. 3. Decorate the faces with different patterns or emojis. 4. Ensure the folds allow the toy to "rotate" or "flip" infinitely. 5. Use it as a tactile tool to keep hands busy and focused.

title: pixelart
instructions: 1. Look at low-resolution digital images. 2. Use graph paper where each square represents one "pixel." 3. Fill in squares with solid colors to create a character or object. 4. Avoid diagonal lines; only use vertical and horizontal blocks. 5. Try to create a recognizable face using the fewest squares possible.

title: helicopter stories
description: Children tell and act out their stories
instructions: 1. Have a child dictate a story exactly as they tell it. 2. Read the story aloud to a group. 3. Invite the child (and friends) to act out the story as it is read. 4. Focus on the child's original words without correcting grammar. 5. Encourage creative movement to represent the characters' actions.

title: sticky note rainbow hunt
description: make a line of 1 each of different coloured sticky notes somewhere and hide 4 more of each colour on something around the house, once they have found one they put it under the one in the row
instructions: 1. Place one "base" sticky note of each color in a row on a wall. 2. Hide 4-5 matching sticky notes of each color around the room. 3. The child must find a hidden note and "match" it by placing it underneath the base note. 4. Continue until all columns are filled. 5. Time the activity to add a challenge.

title: under the leg ball pass
description: sit on the floor with your legs, bent and raised 90 degrees from the floor, see how many times you can pass a ball around your legs before you need to put your legs down
instructions: 1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet lifted. 2. Hold a ball and pass it under one leg, then the other in a "figure 8." 3. Keep your feet off the ground the entire time. 4. Count how many passes you can do before your feet touch. 5. Try passing the ball around both legs simultaneously.

title: poser person
instructions: 1. Trace body parts (limbs, torso, head) on cardboard. 2. Cut them out and poke holes at the joints. 3. Connect the parts using brass fasteners so the person can "pose." 4. Draw clothes or faces on the figure. 5. Use the figure as a reference for drawing different action poses.

title: body part placer
instructions: 1. Draw a large outline of a person on a roll of paper. 2. Create separate cards with the names or drawings of body parts (elbow, knee, lungs). 3. Have children take turns placing the cards on the correct spot on the outline. 4. Discuss what each part does. 5. Use your own body to "find" the parts as you place the cards.

title: drip painting hair
instructions: 1. Place a large dollop of paint at the top of a piece of paper. 2. Prop the paper up vertically to let the paint drip down. 3. Use a straw to blow the drips in different directions. 4. Layer different colors to see them blend as they fall. 5. Once dry, draw faces at the top of the drips so the paint looks like colorful hair.

title: egg box teddy bears
what you'll need: Egg carton, glue, paint, cotton balls
instructions: 1. Cut two cups out of an egg carton. 2. Glue them together to form the head and body. 3. Use the "humps" for ears or paws. 4. Paint the carton brown or white. 5. Glue a small cotton ball to the back for a tail and draw on a face.

title: draw your own articulated figurines
instructions: 1. Draw a person or animal in sections (head, arms, legs). 2. Cut the sections out. 3. Overlap the joints and secure with a brass fastener. 4. Move the limbs to see how the figure can sit, run, or wave. 5. Use these as characters for a stop-motion video or a puppet show.

title: pipe cleaner hand puppets
instructions: 1. Wrap a pipe cleaner around your finger to create a spiral. 2. Slide the spiral off; this is the body. 3. Glue googly eyes and a pom-pom "nose" to the top. 4. Add smaller pipe cleaner pieces for ears or arms. 5. Put them on your fingers and put on a play.

title: egg box reef
what you'll need: Egg cartons, green/blue paint, glitter, scraps
instructions: 1. Use the bottom of a large egg carton as the "seabed." 2. Cut individual cups and trim the edges to look like anemones or coral. 3. Paint everything in vibrant "underwater" colors. 4. Glue in small pebbles or blue paper scraps for water. 5. Add paper fish or pipe cleaner seaweed to complete the reef.

title: salt dough
what you'll need: 2 cups flour, 1 cup salt, 1 cup water
instructions: 1. Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. 2. Gradually add water while stirring until it reaches a dough-like consistency. 3. Knead for 5-10 minutes until smooth. 4. Model the dough into shapes or ornaments. 5. Air dry for several days or bake at a low temperature until hard.

title: mini gardens
what you'll need: Small containers, soil, seeds, tiny decorations
instructions: 1. Fill a small pot or tray with soil. 2. Plant quick-growing seeds like cress or grass. 3. Add "fairy garden" elements like small stones or stick fences. 4. Water the garden gently every day. 5. Observe how the "landscape" changes as the plants grow.

title: toilet roll tube fish
what you'll need: Toilet paper roll, paint, paper, scissors
instructions: 1. Paint a cardboard tube a bright color. 2. Once dry, squash one end of the tube and staple it shut in a "V" shape for the tail. 3. Cut two slits in the sides and insert paper triangles for fins. 4. Draw large eyes on the open end. 5. Decorate with scales using markers or glitter.

title: disappearing picture
what you'll need: Ziploc bag, white paper, black marker, permanent markers
instructions: 1. Draw a picture on white paper with a black marker (e.g., an empty glass). 2. Place the paper inside a Ziploc bag. 3. Use permanent markers to draw "on" the bag (e.g., fill the glass with orange juice). 4. Dip the bag into a container of water at an angle. 5. The white paper will seem to disappear, leaving only the drawing on the bag visible.

title: tiger puppet
what you'll need: Paper bag or cardstock, orange/black markers, glue
instructions: 1. Use an orange paper bag as the base. 2. Draw black stripes all over the bag. 3. Cut out ears and a long tail from orange paper and glue them on. 4. Create a "mouth" in the fold of the bag. 5. Stick your hand in and make the tiger roar.

title: cardboard construction
instructions: 1. Collect boxes of different sizes. 2. Cut "slots" into the sides of the cardboard. 3. Slide the cardboard pieces together to build walls and towers without glue. 4. Use tape only for reinforcing heavy joints. 5. Build a structure large enough to sit inside.

title: lolly stick circle game
instructions: 1. Write numbers or draw shapes on the ends of lolly sticks. 2. Place them face down in a circle. 3. Players take turns flipping two sticks. 4. If the sticks match (e.g., both have a square), the player keeps them. 5. Continue until all "matches" are found.

title: kinetic sand
what you'll need: 9 cups sand, 3 cups cornstarch, 1.5 cups water
instructions: 1. Mix the sand and cornstarch thoroughly in a large bin. 2. Add water and stir until the mixture is crumbly but holds its shape when squeezed. 3. Add a few drops of dish soap to make it extra soft. 4. Use molds to build towers. 5. Watch how the sand "flows" when you break the structure.

title: paper weaving
instructions: 1. Fold a piece of paper in half and cut slits from the fold, stopping an inch from the edge. 2. Cut strips of a different colored paper. 3. Weave the strips through the slits in an "over-under" pattern. 4. Push the strips close together. 5. Glue the ends of the strips to the edges of the base paper to secure the design.

title: dino race spelling
what you'll need: Toy dinosaurs, letter tiles or cards
instructions: 1. Lay out a "track" of letters on the floor. 2. Give each child a dinosaur. 3. Call out a simple word (e.g., "CAT"). 4. The children must move their dinosaur to each letter of the word in the correct order. 5. The first dinosaur to finish the word wins the round.

title: flubber
what you'll need: 1.5 cups warm water, 2 cups white glue, 1.5 cups warm water (separate), 3 tbsp Borax
instructions: 1. Mix 2 cups glue with 1.5 cups water and food coloring. 2. In a separate bowl, dissolve Borax in 1.5 cups warm water. 3. Slowly pour the Borax solution into the glue mixture. 4. Reach in and pull the mass out, kneading it until it is smooth and rubbery. 5. Unlike slime, "flubber" is tougher and bounces higher.

title: wave picture
what you'll need: Paper, blue and white paint, cardboard scrap
instructions: 1. Place dots of blue and white paint at the bottom of a page. 2. Use a straight edge of cardboard to "drag" the paint upward in a wavy motion. 3. The colors will swirl together to look like ocean waves. 4. Add "foam" by dabbing white paint with a sponge at the top of the waves. 5. Let dry and add paper boats.
variations: make waves more pointy so it can be folded like a card

title: bioplastic suncatchers
what you'll need: Gelatin, glycerin, water, food coloring, molds
instructions: 1. Mix gelatin and water, then heat until dissolved. 2. Add glycerin to make the plastic flexible. 3. Pour into shallow molds or onto a flat tray. 4. Let it set until firm. 5. Peel the "plastic" shapes off and stick them to a window; the light will shine through like stained glass.

title: cookie counting
what you'll need: Brown paper/cardboard, black marker, small blocks or "chocolate chips"
instructions: 1. Cut circles out of brown paper to look like cookies. 2. Write a number (1-10) on each cookie. 3. Have the child identify the number. 4. Place that exact number of "chips" (buttons or blocks) onto the cookie. 5. Repeat until all cookies are "baked."

title: fingerprint birds on a line
what you'll need: Ink pad or paint, markers, paper
instructions: 1. Draw several horizontal lines across a paper to look like power lines. 2. Dip a finger into paint and press it onto the lines. 3. Once the fingerprints are dry, use a fine marker to draw beaks, wings, and legs on the prints. 4. Make some birds looking up and some looking down. 5. Count how many birds are "sitting" on the wire.

title: animal pattern match
instructions: 1. Collect images of animal skins (zebra stripes, leopard spots, giraffe patches). 2. Create a set of cards showing the full animal. 3. Lay the pattern cards face up. 4. Have children match the animal card to its corresponding skin pattern. 5. Discuss how these patterns help the animals hide (camouflage).

title: face jumble
instructions: 1. Cut out eyes, noses, and mouths from different magazine photos. 2. Mix them all up in a bowl. 3. Glue the parts onto a blank face template to create a "jumble" person. 4. Discuss how the different features change the "emotion" of the face. 5. Try to make a face that looks happy, sad, or surprised.

title: egg box crocodile
what you'll need: Two egg cartons, green paint, glue, paper
instructions: 1. Paint two long egg cartons green. 2. Glue them end-to-end for a very long body. 3. Cut out "teeth" from white paper and glue them along the edge of the front carton. 4. Use two humps from a spare carton as eyes. 5. Add a long paper tail at the back.

title: string art
instructions: 1. Cut a shape out of cardboard and cut small notches around the edge. 2. Tape the end of a piece of yarn to the back. 3. Wrap the yarn from notch to notch across the front of the shape. 4. Change colors to create a layered effect. 5. Secure the final end on the back with tape.

title: string paths
what you'll need: Long pieces of string or yarn
instructions: 1. Lay strings on the floor in winding, zigzag, or straight patterns. 2. Have children "walk the tightrope" by staying exactly on the string. 3. Change the movement: hop along the string, or walk backward. 4. Create a "web" of strings for children to crawl through without touching. 5. Use different colors to signify different paths.

title: roll to join the dots
instructions: 1. Draw 20-30 numbered dots randomly across a page. 2. Roll a die. 3. Draw a line to connect that many dots (e.g., if you roll a 3, connect dots 1, 2, and 3). 4. Take turns until all dots are connected to form a mystery shape. 5. Color in the resulting "constellation."

title: cd case tracing
what you'll need: Clear CD case, dry erase markers, flashlight
instructions: 1. Open a clear CD case and stand it up. 2. Place a drawing behind the case. 3. Use a marker to trace the drawing onto the plastic surface. 4. Remove the original drawing and place a flashlight behind the case. 5. Watch the "traced" image project onto a nearby wall.

title: mirror trace
instructions: 1. Draw half of a simple shape (like a butterfly or a heart) on a piece of paper. 2. Place a handheld mirror vertically along the center line of the drawing. 3. Look into the mirror to see the "complete" shape. 4. Try to draw the second half of the shape while looking only at the mirror's reflection. 5. Discuss how the mirror "flips" the image.

title: paper plate seagulls
what you'll need: Paper plate, blue/gray paint, yellow paper
instructions: 1. Paint a paper plate white or light gray. 2. Fold the plate in half. 3. Cut two long, thin triangles from another plate or cardstock for wings and glue them to the sides. 4. Cut a small yellow triangle for a beak and glue it to the front. 5. Draw an eye and hang the seagull from a string so it "flies."

title: egg box seal
what you'll need: Egg carton, gray paint, cotton balls
instructions: 1. Cut a single cup out of an egg carton for the head and two for the body. 2. Paint them gray. 3. Use the carton "flaps" to create flippers. 4. Glue a small gray-painted cotton ball on the front for a snout. 5. Draw on whiskers and eyes.

title: car pens
what you'll need: Toy cars, markers, tape, large paper
instructions: 1. Tape a marker to the back or side of a toy car so the tip touches the floor. 2. Lay out a large sheet of paper. 3. Drive the cars around the paper in circles, zigzags, and races. 4. Observe the "path" the cars leave behind. 5. Use different colored markers for different cars to see where they intersected.

title: moon sand
instructions: 1. Mix the flour and oil in a large bin. 2. Use your hands to incorporate the oil until the flour feels soft and moldable. 3. Squeeze a handful; it should hold its shape like wet sand. 4. Poke it; it should crumble back into "dust." 5. Add sand toys for open-ended sensory play.

title: lion mane paper craft
what you'll need: Paper plate, orange paint, brown paper strips
instructions: 1. Paint a paper plate bright orange. 2. Cut many thin strips of brown or yellow paper. 3. Glue the strips all around the edge of the plate to create a "shaggy" mane. 4. Draw a lion's face in the center of the plate. 5. Add ears made of paper scraps at the top.

title: egg box penguins
what you'll need: Egg carton, black/white paint, orange paper
instructions: 1. Cut individual cups from an egg carton. 2. Paint the front white and the rest black. 3. Cut a tiny orange triangle for a beak and glue it on. 4. Glue on small black paper "flippers." 5. Stand them up in a group to create a penguin colony.

title: toilet roll racecar
what you'll need: Toilet paper roll, 4 bottle caps, straws, skewers
instructions: 1. Paint a toilet paper roll your favorite racing color. 2. Poke two holes through the sides of the roll at the front and back. 3. Slide straws through the holes, then skewers through the straws. 4. Attach bottle caps to the ends of the skewers as wheels. 5. Cut a small "U" shape in the top for a cockpit and add a paper driver.

title: haircutting game
instructions: 1. Draw a face on a sheet of paper. 2. Cut vertical strips above the forehead to act as "hair." 3. Draw dotted lines or shapes on the hair strips. 4. Have the child use scissors to "cut" the hair along the lines. 5. Experiment with different "hairstyles" like fringes or mohawks.

title: inching caterpillar
instructions: 1. Fold a thin strip of paper into an accordion shape. 2. Round the corners to look like a caterpillar. 3. Place the caterpillar on a smooth surface. 4. Use a straw to blow air directly at the top of the middle fold. 5. The caterpillar will "inch" forward as the air pressure changes.

title: connect the dots rocket
instructions: 1. Draw a series of numbered dots that form a rocket ship. 2. Have the child connect the dots in numerical order. 3. Discuss the "countdown" sequence from the highest number down to one. 4. Color in the rocket once the outline is complete. 5. Add "fire" at the bottom with orange and red markers.

title: peg animals
instructions: 1. Draw small animal bodies (without legs) on cardstock. 2. Cut out the bodies and color them. 3. Clip two wooden pegs to the bottom of each body to act as legs. 4. The pegs allow the animals to stand upright. 5. Move the pegs to make the animals "walk" or "jump."

title: animal rescue
instructions: 1. Place several plastic toy animals on a tray. 2. Use strips of masking tape to "trap" the animals to the surface. 3. Provide the child with the mission to "rescue" the animals. 4. The child must carefully peel back the tape to free each one. 5. Discuss how to be gentle with animals during the rescue.

title: drawing dice
instructions: 1. Assign a body part or feature to each number on a die (e.g., 1 = eyes, 2 = ears). 2. Take turns rolling the die. 3. Draw the assigned feature on your "monster" or "person" based on the roll. 4. Continue until everyone has a complete, unique drawing. 5. Compare the results to see how the die influenced the art.

title: bead snake
instructions: 1. Start with a green bead for the snake's head. 2. Create a pattern (e.g., Red-Yellow-Red-Yellow). 3. Slide the beads onto a pipe cleaner according to the pattern. 4. Bend the end of the pipe cleaner to secure the beads. 5. Use the snake to "measure" objects around the room.

title: eat and excrete
what you'll need: Ziploc bag, crackers, water, orange juice (acid), stocking
instructions: 1. Place crackers in a bag and crush them (chewing). 2. Add water (saliva) and orange juice (stomach acid). 3. Squeeze the bag to mix. 4. Pour the mixture into a stocking (small intestine) and squeeze the liquid out. 5. Push the remaining solid through a hole at the end to demonstrate excretion.

title: pen push
instructions: 1. Place a mug on the table. 2. Hold a pen vertically over the mug at waist height. 3. Try to drop the pen so it lands inside the mug. 4. Increase the difficulty by standing further away or using a smaller container. 5. Use different weights of pens to see how they fall.

title: sand mousse
instructions: 1. Pour sand into a large mixing bowl. 2. Add a large amount of shaving cream. 3. Mix by hand until the texture is light and "moussy." 4. Use it to build "soft" towers or draw patterns with fingers. 5. Observe how the mixture feels different from standard wet sand.

title: fire breathing dragon
what you'll need: Toilet paper roll, tissue paper, glue, markers
instructions: 1. Paint a cardboard tube green. 2. Glue googly eyes and pom-poms (nostrils) to one end. 3. Glue long strips of red and orange tissue paper inside the other end. 4. Blow through the eye-end of the tube. 5. Watch the "fire" flutter as the dragon breathes.

title: 2 player paper basketball game
description: this is for children to play with, I am not expecting them to be able to make it themselves.
what you'll need: Cardboard, paper cups, rubber bands, ping pong ball
instructions: 1. Build a small hoop using a paper cup with the bottom cut out. 2. Attach a cardboard "lever" powered by a rubber band. 3. Place a small ball on the lever. 4. Press and release to launch the ball toward the hoop. 5. Take turns and keep score like a real basketball game.

title: colour smashing under clingfilm
instructions: 1. Place several drops of different colored paint on a piece of paper. 2. Carefully cover the entire paper with a layer of clingfilm. 3. Have the child "smash" and spread the paint through the plastic with their fingers. 4. Observe the colors blending without getting hands messy. 5. Peel back the film to see the final textured masterpiece.

title: paperchainsnake
instructions: 1. Cut paper into thin strips. 2. Loop one strip and glue the ends to make a ring. 3. Thread the next strip through the ring and glue it to start a chain. 4. Repeat until the "snake" is long. 5. Add a paper head with a flicking tongue at one end.

title: frog and fly
description: could use as cup and ball
instructions: 1. Decorate a paper cup to look like a frog's face. 2. Tie a string to a small paper "fly" or bead. 3. Attach the other end of the string to the bottom of the cup. 4. Hold the cup and toss the fly into the air. 5. Try to catch the fly inside the "frog's mouth" (the cup).

title: tennis ball monster
what you'll need: Old tennis ball, googly eyes, utility knife
instructions: 1. Carefully cut a horizontal slit (a "mouth") in a tennis ball. 2. Glue googly eyes above the slit. 3. Squeeze the sides of the ball to make the "monster" open its mouth. 4. Feed the monster small items like beads, coins, or beans. 5. This strengthens the hand muscles needed for writing.

title: floppy fish
instructions: 1. Fold a piece of paper into a "floppy" accordion shape. 2. Draw a fish on the top layer. 3. Hold the paper by the tail and wiggle it. 4. The "floppy" folds make the fish look like it is swimming through water. 5. Experiment with different lengths to see which swims best.

title: chopstick/tweezer fishing
what you'll need: Chopsticks or tweezers, small toys, bowl of water
instructions: 1. Place small waterproof toys (plastic fish, beads) in a bowl of water. 2. Provide the child with chopsticks or large tweezers. 3. The child must "fish" the items out and move them to a dry tray. 4. Use different sizes of objects to vary the difficulty. 5. Time the activity for a competitive "fishing" game.

title: shark pop-up card
instructions: 1. Fold a piece of cardstock in half. 2. Cut two parallel slits in the center of the fold to create a "mouth" tab. 3. Push the tab inward so it pops out when the card opens. 4. Decorate the tab to look like a shark's mouth with sharp teeth. 5. Add the rest of the shark's body around the mouth.

title: woodpecker absailor
instructions: 1. Draw and cut out a small woodpecker. 2. Tape a small piece of straw to the back of the bird. 3. Thread a long string through the straw and tie it vertically between two points. 4. Hold the string slightly loose. 5. Jerk the string to make the woodpecker "absail" or peck its way down the line.

title: painting flowers
instructions: 1. Dip the "face" of a fresh flower (like a daisy or mum) into thick paint. 2. Press the flower onto a sheet of paper like a stamp. 3. Observe the unique patterns created by the petals. 4. Use different types of flowers to create a "garden" print. 5. Add stems and leaves with a paintbrush.

title: cardboard gymnast
instructions: 1. Cut a person shape out of cardboard with separate arms and legs. 2. Connect the limbs with brass fasteners at the "shoulders" and "hips." 3. Attach strings to the hands and feet. 4. Pull the strings to make the gymnast perform flips or poses. 5. Discuss how the pivot points allow for movement.

title: hairdressers
instructions: 1. Set up a "salon" station with a mirror and chairs. 2. Provide dolls or willing volunteers as "customers." 3. Use spray bottles with water to "prep" the hair. 4. Practice combing, braiding, and adding clips or ribbons. 5. Discuss the steps of a haircut and how to sit still.

title: frog handwriting helper
what you'll need: Small frog toy or cut-out, pencil
instructions: 1. Attach a small frog to the top of a pencil. 2. Tell the child the frog needs to "watch" them write. 3. The weight of the toy encourages the child to hold the pencil lower. 4. Use the "frog's legs" as a guide for finger placement (tripod grip). 5. Practice drawing "lily pads" (circles) to warm up.

title: lollystick ladders
instructions: 1. Lay two lolly sticks parallel on the table. 2. Glue "rungs" horizontally across the two sticks. 3. Wait for the glue to dry. 4. See how many "steps" high you can make the ladder. 5. Test if the ladder can support the weight of a small toy figure.

title: light sabres
description: I would like to say that I am not encouraging anyone to hit anything with these. They are purely about the sensory input from the lights.
what you'll need: Empty plastic bottle, glow sticks, water, glitter
instructions: 1. Activate several glow sticks and place them inside a clear bottle. 2. Fill the rest of the bottle with water and a pinch of glitter. 3. Seal the cap tightly with glue. 4. Shake the bottle to see the light diffuse through the water. 5. Use in a dark room to observe the "sabre" glow without any physical impact.

title: tube climber
instructions: 1. Decorate a cardboard tube as a "climber." 2. Thread a long string through the tube. 3. Tie a bead to the bottom of the string so the tube doesn't slide off. 4. Hold the top of the string and tilt it. 5. Watch the tube "climb" or slide depending on the angle and tension.

title: dino excavation
what you'll need: Plaster of Paris, sand, plastic dinosaurs
instructions: 1. Mix sand and plaster with water. 2. Bury plastic dinosaurs in the mixture inside a container. 3. Let it dry until it is a hard block. 4. Give the child a small brush and a "digging tool" (like a lolly stick). 5. Carefully excavate the dinosaurs without breaking them.

title: growing flower
instructions: 1. Draw a flower on a small piece of paper. 2. Fold the petals inward toward the center. 3. Place the "bud" in a shallow dish of water. 4. Observe as the paper fibers absorb water, causing the petals to "bloom" and open. 5. Discuss how real plants use water to grow and stand tall.

title: shadow puppets
instructions: 1. Cut character silhouettes out of black cardstock. 2. Tape each silhouette to a wooden skewer. 3. Hang a white sheet and place a flashlight behind it. 4. Hold the puppets between the light and the sheet. 5. Move the puppets closer to the light to make the shadows grow larger.

title: junk modelling jet pack/scuba tank
what you'll need: Two large plastic bottles, silver paint, tape, straps
instructions: 1. Paint two 2-liter bottles silver. 2. Tape them together side-by-side. 3. Attach ribbon or elastic "straps" so the bottles can be worn like a backpack. 4. Add "flames" (orange tissue paper) for a jet pack, or a "hose" (yarn) for a scuba tank. 5. Use for imaginative play in outer space or under the sea.

title: walking feet
instructions: 1. Trace your feet onto paper and cut them out. 2. Tape the "feet" to the floor in a path. 3. Vary the angles—some toes pointing left, some right, some together. 4. The child must jump or step to match the "walking feet" on the floor. 5. Increase the speed as they get better at the coordination.

title: foil shadows
instructions: 1. Crumple a piece of foil, then flatten it out slightly. 2. Shine a flashlight on the foil at an angle. 3. Observe the "shimmering" shadows cast on a nearby wall or paper. 4. Draw around the shapes created by the light. 5. Discuss how the uneven surface of the foil reflects light in many directions.

title: sponge sailboats
what you'll need: Kitchen sponges, lolly sticks, paper (for sails)
instructions: 1. Cut a small slit in the top of a sponge. 2. Insert a lolly stick to act as a mast. 3. Tape a paper triangle (the sail) to the stick. 4. Place the "boat" in a tub of water. 5. Blow on the sail to make the boat travel across the "ocean."

title: drawing shadows
instructions: 1. Place a toy or object on the ground in the sun. 2. Use chalk to trace the shadow it casts on the pavement. 3. Return every hour and trace the shadow again. 4. Observe how the shadow moves and changes length as the sun moves. 5. Discuss why the shadow is longest in the morning and evening.

title: guess the footprint
instructions: 1. Flatten several "pancakes" of play dough. 2. Press the feet of different toy animals into the dough. 3. Mix up the animals. 4. Ask the child to "guess the footprint" by matching the animal to its track. 5. Discuss how scientists use tracks to track animals in the wild.

title: hot air balloon
instructions: 1. Blow up a balloon. 2. Attach four strings to the balloon and tie them to a small paper cup (the basket). 3. Place a small toy "passenger" in the basket. 4. Discuss how hot air balloons work using hot air to rise. 5. Toss the balloon into the air and watch it drift slowly to the ground.

title: butterfly spinner
instructions: 1. Cut a butterfly shape out of cardstock. 2. Decorate both sides with vibrant colors. 3. Poke a toothpick through the center of the butterfly. 4. Spin the toothpick like a top. 5. Observe how the colors blend together as the butterfly "spins."

title: coloured water bubbles
what you'll need: Water, dish soap, food coloring, straw
instructions: 1. Mix water with a squeeze of dish soap and food coloring. 2. Use a straw to blow bubbles into the mixture until they overflow. 3. Gently press a piece of paper onto the bubbles. 4. The popping bubbles create a unique circular pattern on the paper. 5. Use different colors to create a "bubble rainbow."

title: tortoise and hare racers
instructions: 1. Create a "race track" on the floor using tape. 2. Place a toy tortoise and a toy hare at the start. 3. Move the tortoise slowly and the hare quickly. 4. Discuss the fable of the Tortoise and the Hare. 5. Have children "act out" the race using slow and fast movements.

title: paperplate astronaut helmets
instructions: 1. Cut a large circle out of the center of a paper plate. 2. Paint the plate silver. 3. Tape a layer of clingfilm over the hole to act as the "visor." 4. Decorate with "buttons" or NASA logos. 5. Hold it up to your face to become an astronaut on a space mission.

title: day and night
instructions: 1. Cut a large circle and a slightly smaller circle from paper. 2. Draw a "sun" and daytime scene on one half of the large circle, and a "moon" and night scene on the other. 3. Cut a "window" out of the smaller circle. 4. Connect the two in the center with a split pin. 5. Rotate the wheel to show the transition from day to night.

title: grabber
instructions: 1. Connect lolly sticks in an "X" pattern using brass fasteners. 2. Connect several "X" shapes to create an extendable arm. 3. Attach cardboard "claws" to the end. 4. Pull the bottom handles to make the grabber reach out. 5. Practice picking up soft pom-poms or empty cups.

title: papercup woodpecker
instructions: 1. Tie a string to a toothpick and poke it through the bottom of a cup. 2. Wet the string with a damp cloth. 3. Pull your fingers down the string in short jerks. 4. The friction creates a "pecking" or "chirping" sound that is amplified by the cup. 5. Decorate the cup to look like a woodpecker.

title: egg box boat
what you'll need: Egg carton, lolly stick, paper, glue
instructions: 1. Cut a section of an egg carton to be the "hull." 2. Glue a lolly stick vertically into one of the cups. 3. Attach a paper sail to the stick. 4. Paint the boat to look like a pirate ship or a rowboat. 5. Test it in a bowl of water to see if it stays upright.

title: boat making challange/experiment
what you'll need: Various household materials (foil, plastic, wood, cork)
instructions: 1. Challenge the child to build a boat that can hold 10 "passengers" (pennies). 2. Provide a variety of materials. 3. Let the child experiment with different shapes and materials. 4. Test each design in water. 5. Discuss why some designs floated better or held more weight than others.

title: dino headdress
instructions: 1. Cut several large triangles out of cardboard. 2. Paint them green. 3. Tape the triangles to a strip of cardboard that fits around the head. 4. Ensure the "spikes" stand up straight. 5. Wear the headdress and stomp around like a dinosaur.

title: animals fingerprint art
instructions: 1. Use thumbprints to create animal bodies (e.g., a round body for a pig, a long one for a caterpillar). 2. Use a fine-tip marker to add details like ears, tails, and legs. 3. Create a whole "zoo" of fingerprint animals. 4. Discuss how everyone's fingerprints are unique. 5. Count how many different animals you can make.

title: bouncing bunnies
instructions: 1. Cut two small slits in the rim of a paper cup. 2. Hook a rubber band across the slits. 3. Place another cup inside the first one, pushing down on the rubber band. 4. Release! 5. The "bunny" (cup) will bounce into the air as the rubber band releases its energy.

title: balance bird
instructions: 1. Cut a bird shape out of cardstock, ensuring the "beak" is a sharp point. 2. Tape a penny to the underside of each wingtip. 3. Place the beak of the bird on the tip of your finger. 4. The weights in the wings move the center of gravity forward, allowing the bird to "balance" on your finger. 5. Gently tap the bird to see it wobble without falling.

title: indoor woggle obstacle course
instructions: 1. Use pool noodles to create "tunnels" by taping them in arcs to the floor. 2. Create "hurdles" by resting noodles between two chairs. 3. Lay noodles in a line for a "balance beam." 4. Have the child complete the course as fast as they can. 5. Rearrange the course to keep it challenging.

title: handwriting warmup
instructions: 1. "Spider on a mirror": touch fingertips together and move them. 2. "Piano player": tap fingers on the table rapidly. 3. "The O": touch each finger to the thumb one by one. 4. "Squeeze": make a tight fist and then stretch fingers wide. 5. These movements prepare the hand muscles for the precision of writing.

title: salt dough dino fossils
what you'll need: 2 cups flour, 1 cup salt, 1 cup used coffee grounds, water
instructions: 1. Mix dry ingredients (coffee grounds make it look like "dirt"). 2. Add water until it becomes a thick dough. 3. Press plastic dinosaurs into the dough to leave a footprint. 4. Remove the dinosaur and bake the dough at a low temperature. 5. The result is a hard "fossil" that looks like it was dug up from the ground.

title: combining tracing with backgrounds using slippery fish
instructions: 1. Trace around your hand on blue paper. 2. Turn the paper sideways; the fingers are now the "tail" and fins of a "slippery fish." 3. Draw a large eye and a mouth on the "palm" part. 4. Add "bubbles" using a white crayon. 5. Draw a coral reef background for the fish to swim in.

title: count and feed
instructions: 1. Create a cardboard box with a large "mouth" cut out. 2. Roll a die. 3. "Feed" the monster that exact number of pom-poms. 4. Count out loud as you place each one in the mouth. 5. Empty the monster and play again.

title: spiderman poser
instructions: 1. Trace the parts of Spiderman (torso, mask, limbs) on cardboard. 2. Color them in the classic suit patterns. 3. Use brass fasteners to connect the joints. 4. Pose the figure in iconic "web-swinging" or "crawling" positions. 5. Discuss how Spiderman uses his muscles to move.

title: starry night
what you'll need: Blue paper, yellow and white paint, forks/brushes
instructions: 1. Look at Van Gogh's "Starry Night." 2. Use a fork to swirl yellow paint in circular motions on blue paper to create "stars." 3. Add white "wind" swirls. 4. Draw a dark silhouette of a town or tree at the bottom. 5. Discuss how the swirly lines make the painting feel like it is moving.

title: totter dinos
instructions: 1. Cut out a dinosaur shape. 2. Tape pennies to the "tail" and "head" to find the perfect balance point. 3. Place the dinosaur on the edge of a table. 4. Adjust the weight until it "totters" but doesn't fall off. 5. Discuss how long tails helped dinosaurs balance their heavy bodies.

title: big beaks
instructions: 1. Draw a bird face on a piece of paper. 2. Cut a long, wide strip of paper. 3. Fold the strip in half and glue only the edges to the face to create a "3D" protruding beak. 4. Decorate the beak with bright colors. 5. Add "feathers" by fringing the edges of the paper.

title: milking cows
what you'll need: Rubber glove, water (or milk), pin, bowl
instructions: 1. Fill a rubber glove with water and tie the end shut. 2. Poke a tiny hole in the tip of one or two fingers with a pin. 3. Have the child hold the "udder" over a bowl. 4. Gently squeeze the fingers in a downward motion to "milk" the glove. 5. Discuss where milk comes from and the process of farming.

title: beach busy book
what you'll need: Binder or notebook, sand, shells, fabric (water), photos
instructions: 1. Create a "Beach" themed page in a busy book. 2. Glue down a patch of sandpaper for "sand." 3. Use blue silk or felt for "waves." 4. Add "seek and find" elements like small flat shells hidden under the fabric. 5. Use the book to talk about what we see and do at the seaside.

title: talking pirates
what you'll need: Paper bag, black paper, googly eyes
instructions: 1. Use a black paper bag (or paint one) as the base. 2. Glue on an eyepatch and a "hat" cut from paper. 3. Draw a mustache and a scar. 4. Use the fold of the bag as the mouth. 5. Talk like a pirate and tell stories of hidden treasure.

title: ice tower
description: WARNING: DO NOT TOUCH THE ICE AS IT IS REACTING WITH THE SALT, IT WILL BURN YOU. DO NOT LEAVE CHILD ALONE WITH SALT AND ICE.
instructions: 1. Fill a jar with ice and a little water. 2. Pour a large amount of salt over the ice. 3. Observe as the temperature drops rapidly (well below freezing). 4. Use a thermometer to watch the numbers go down. 5. **WARNING**: Do not touch the ice/salt mixture with bare skin, as it can cause "salt burns."

title: face trace
instructions: 1. Have the child stand in front of a mirror. 2. Use a dry-erase marker to trace the outline of their own face directly onto the mirror. 3. Trace the eyes, nose, and mouth. 4. Step away to see the "self-portrait" left on the glass. 5. Wipe clean and try again with different expressions (happy, silly).

title: under the sea fingerprint art
instructions: 1. Use fingerprints to create "underwater" scenes (fish, crabs, bubbles). 2. Use the side of the thumb for a whale and the tip for a school of small fish. 3. Draw "seaweed" with green markers. 4. Add "waves" at the top of the page. 5. Discuss the different creatures that live in the ocean.

title: pencil grip bracelet
instructions: 1. Slide a rubber band onto the child's wrist. 2. Twist the band into a figure-8 and slide the pencil through the second loop. 3. This gently pulls the pencil back into the "crook" of the hand. 4. It helps children who struggle to keep the pencil from standing too upright. 5. Practice writing your name with the "brace."

title: mini dino dig
what you'll need: Small container, sand, tiny plastic dinosaurs
instructions: 1. Hide 5-10 tiny dinosaurs in a small bowl of sand. 2. Provide a paintbrush. 3. The child must "dust" away the sand to find each dinosaur. 4. Once found, sort the dinosaurs by type or color. 5. Discuss how real paleontologists have to be very patient.

title: reel in the fish
what you'll need: Paper fish, string, lolly stick, magnet, paperclip
instructions: 1. Attach a paperclip to several paper fish. 2. Tie a string to a lolly stick and glue a magnet to the end. 3. "Cast" your line into a "pond" (a blue rug or box). 4. Use the magnet to catch the fish. 5. Reel them in by winding the string around the stick.

title: 3d shape pull
instructions: 1. Cut out 2D shapes (circle, square, triangle). 2. Poke a hole in the center. 3. Thread a string through the hole. 4. Pull the string to see how the shape looks from different angles. 5. Discuss how a circle can look like a line when turned sideways.

title: buckwheat animal search
what you'll need: Bin of buckwheat (or dried beans), small toy animals
instructions: 1. Fill a tray with buckwheat. 2. Bury 5-10 toy animals deep in the grains. 3. Have the child close their eyes and reach in to find an animal. 4. Just by feeling, can they guess which animal it is? 5. Open eyes to check and repeat.

title: cardboard marble maze
instructions: 1. Glue lolly sticks to the inside of a shallow box to create "walls." 2. Create a path from a "start" to a "finish" hole. 3. Add obstacles like "dead ends." 4. Place a marble at the start. 5. Tilt the box to guide the marble through the maze without getting stuck.

title: nature bracelets
instructions: 1. Wrap a piece of duct tape around the child's wrist with the sticky side facing out. 2. Go for a walk in a garden or park. 3. Pick up fallen petals, leaves, or interesting grass. 4. Stick them onto the "bracelet" to create a piece of wearable nature art. 5. Discuss the different textures and colors collected.

title: cup and ball
instructions: 1. Decorate a paper cup. 2. Poke a hole in the bottom and thread a string through, tying a knot inside. 3. Tie a large bead or ball to the other end of the string. 4. Swing the cup to catch the bead inside. 5. Practice until you can do it 5 times in a row.

title: cd rainbows
instructions: 1. Shine a flashlight onto the shiny side of an old CD. 2. Reflect the light onto a white piece of paper. 3. Observe the "rainbow" (spectrum) that appears. 4. Move the CD to see how the colors change and dance. 5. Discuss how the tiny grooves in the CD split the white light into colors.

title: dinosaur hatch
instructions: 1. Place a tiny toy dinosaur inside a plastic egg. 2. Fill the egg with water and freeze it. 3. Once frozen, remove the plastic shell to have a "dino egg." 4. Provide the child with warm water and a dropper. 5. "Hatch" the dinosaur by melting the ice.

title: elastic windmill
description: this is for children to play with, I am not expecting them to be able to make it themselves.
instructions: 1. Build a basic "windmill" frame from cardboard. 2. Use a twisted rubber band to create a "motor." 3. Wind up the blades. 4. Release to see the windmill spin on its own. 5. Discuss how the "stretch" of the rubber band stores energy.

title: paper cup pedal bins
instructions: 1. Cut a small "door" at the bottom of a paper cup. 2. Build a cardboard "pedal" that connects to a hinge inside. 3. When you step on the pedal, the lid of the bin (another piece of cardboard) pops open. 4. Use it for small scraps of paper at your desk. 5. Discuss how levers help us do work.

title: easy diy puffy/squishy paint
what you'll need: Shaving cream, white glue, food coloring
instructions: 1. Mix equal parts shaving cream and white glue. 2. Add food coloring. 3. Paint a picture (like an ice cream cone or a cloud) with the thick mixture. 4. Let it dry overnight. 5. The paint will stay "puffy" and squishy to the touch even when dry.

title: shadow frogs
instructions: 1. Shine a flashlight on a wall. 2. Hold a paper frog between the light and the wall. 3. Move the frog closer to the light—the shadow gets huge! 4. Move it further away—the shadow gets small. 5. Discuss how the distance from the light source affects the shadow's size.

title: lollystick angelfish
instructions: 1. Glue three lolly sticks into a triangle for the body. 2. Add two more sticks for the "tail" fins. 3. Paint the fish bright colors. 4. Add a googly eye. 5. Group them together to show a "school" of fish.

title: paper crumple for hand strength
instructions: 1. Give the child a single sheet of paper. 2. Using only one hand, they must crumple the paper into the smallest ball possible. 3. Now, using only that same hand, they must try to flatten it back out. 4. Switch hands and repeat. 5. This build intrinsic hand strength for better pencil control.

title: finger strenghtening with play dough
instructions: 1. Hide several small beads inside a large ball of play dough. 2. The child must poke, squeeze, and pull the dough to find all the "treasures." 3. Use the index finger to poke deep holes. 4. Use the thumb and forefinger to "pinch" the dough. 5. This works the specific muscles used for buttoning clothes and zipping.

title: dancing game
instructions: 1. Play music and have everyone dance. 2. When the music stops, everyone must "freeze" in a specific pose (e.g., "freeze like a statue" or "freeze like a bird"). 3. Discuss how our brains tell our bodies to stop and start. 4. Use different speeds of music to change the dance. 5. The last person to freeze is the one who chooses the next pose.

title: accordian fold animals
instructions: 1. Fold a long strip of paper back and forth (accordion style). 2. Draw an animal head on one end and a tail on the other. 3. When you pull the ends, the animal "stretches" out. 4. When you push them, the animal "shrinks." 5. Try making a very long snake or a "growing" dachshund dog.

title: egg box bunny garden
what you'll need: Egg carton, soil, seeds, cotton wool
instructions: 1. Fill egg carton cups with soil. 2. Plant a seed in each "nest." 3. Add a small cotton wool "bunny" decoration. 4. Place in a sunny window and water regularly. 5. Observe which seeds sprout first and create a "mini garden."

title: leaf shadows
instructions: 1. Hold a leaf up to a flashlight. 2. Observe the shadow cast on a piece of paper. 3. Trace the veins of the leaf's shadow. 4. Turn the leaf to see how the shadow changes shape. 5. Discuss why shadows are always dark even if the leaf is green.

title: team drawing
instructions: 1. Have two children hold the same marker. 2. Without talking, they must try to draw a house or a tree together. 3. Observe how they negotiate movement. 4. Try again, but this time they can talk to plan the drawing. 5. Discuss which way was easier and why teamwork is important.

title: leaf printing butterflies
instructions: 1. Paint one side of a large leaf. 2. Press it onto paper, then flip and press it again next to the first print. 3. The two leaf prints create the "wings" of a butterfly. 4. Draw a body and antennae in the middle. 5. Use different shaped leaves for different butterfly wings.

title: bridge building
instructions: 1. Challenge the child to build a bridge between two chairs that can hold a paper cup. 2. Use straws as the main "beams." 3. Experiment with different arrangements (triangles vs. squares). 4. Add "weights" (pennies) to the cup to see when the bridge fails. 5. Redesign the bridge to make it stronger.

title: magic card with disappearing colour
instructions: 1. Draw a colorful scene on a piece of cardstock. 2. Place it inside a Ziploc bag. 3. Draw the same scene in black outline ONLY on the outside of the bag. 4. Dip the bag vertically into water. 5. The color will "disappear" from view, leaving only the black outline. 6. Pull it out to see the color return.

title: racing worms
instructions: 1. Fold a small paper "worm." 2. Use a straw to blow air behind the worm. 3. Race against a friend to see whose worm reaches the finish line first. 4. Try racing on different surfaces (carpet vs. tile). 5. Discuss how the air pushes the paper.

title: tiger fortune teller
instructions: 1. Draw a tiger's face on the outside of a "fortune teller" (cootie catcher). 2. Inside the folds, write "tiger facts" or "tiger actions" (like "ROAR!"). 3. Have a friend pick a color and a number. 4. Open the flap to reveal the action. 5. The player must perform the tiger action.

title: junk modelling aim game
instructions: 1. Cut different sized holes in a large cardboard box. 2. Label each hole with a point value (smaller holes = more points). 3. Stand back and try to toss a ball through the holes. 4. Keep track of your score on a piece of paper. 5. Move further back to make it harder.

title: pringle tube projector
what you'll need: Pringles tube, wax paper, aluminum foil, pin
instructions: 1. Poke a pinhole in the metal bottom of a Pringles tube. 2. Cut a hole in the plastic lid and tape wax paper over it. 3. Point the pinhole at a bright object. 4. Look at the wax paper lid to see a projected image. 5. Discuss how the light travels in straight lines through the pinhole.

title: hologram box
what you'll need: Box, small mirror, flashlight, clear plastic
instructions: 1. Place a mirror at the bottom of a box filled with water. 2. Shine a flashlight onto the mirror. 3. Place a piece of white paper so the reflected light hits it. 4. Observe the "hologram" of colors created on the paper. 5. Discuss how water and light work together.

title: paper cup seasons
instructions: 1. On one cup, draw a tree in four stages (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter). 2. On the second cup, cut a "window." 3. Place the window cup over the tree cup. 4. Rotate the top cup to "watch" the seasons change. 5. Discuss what happens to the weather in each season.

title: campfire
instructions: 1. Collect small sticks from outside. 2. Glue them together in a "tepee" shape on paper. 3. Add red, orange, and yellow tissue paper "flames" in the center. 4. Discuss the "colors of fire." 5. Talk about campfire safety and what we cook on a fire.

title: monster maker
instructions: 1. Start with a blank "monster body." 2. Use a spinner or die to decide which features to add. 3. "Add 3 eyes!" or "Add 2 mouths!" 4. Give the monster a name and a special power. 5. Discuss why your monster looks the way it does.
variations: lots of variation on pinterest e.g. robots, cats

title: paper plate chickens
what you'll need: Paper plate, yellow paint, feathers, paper
instructions: 1. Paint a paper plate yellow and fold it in half. 2. Glue googly eyes and a paper beak to the front. 3. Glue yellow feathers to the back for a tail. 4. Add orange paper "feet" at the bottom. 5. Rock the plate back and forth to make the chicken "walk."

title: pufferfish painting
instructions: 1. Dip a fork into paint. 2. Press the fork in a circular pattern on paper to create "spikes." 3. Fill the circle until it looks like a pufferfish. 4. Add eyes and a mouth in the center. 5. Discuss how pufferfish use their spikes for protection.

title: tissue box monster feet
what you'll need: Two tissue boxes, green paint, markers
instructions: 1. Paint two empty tissue boxes green. 2. Draw "claws" or "scales" on the front. 3. Slide your feet into the openings of the boxes. 4. Walk around like a monster with giant feet. 5. Discuss how big feet help animals balance.

title: wiggling caterpillar
instructions: 1. Fold a paper "caterpillar." 2. Use a straw to blow air onto the "hump" of the caterpillar. 3. Watch it wiggle and move forward. 4. Try making a "long" caterpillar and a "short" one. 5. Which one moves faster?

title: featureswap
what you'll need: Photos of family or friends, scissors, glue
instructions: 1. Print two photos of different people at the same size. 2. Cut both photos in half vertically. 3. Swap the left side of one face with the right side of the other. 4. Glue them down to create a "feature swap" person. 5. Discuss how we share similar features but remain unique individuals.

title: 2 ingredient fake snow
what you'll need: 1 lb Baking soda, 1 can shaving cream
instructions: 1. Pour the baking soda into a large plastic bin. 2. Slowly add shaving cream and mix with your hands. 3. Continue adding cream until the mixture is light, fluffy, and moldable. 4. The "snow" will feel cold to the touch due to the chemical reaction. 5. Use it to build mini snowmen or igloos indoors.

title: horse puppet
instructions: 1. Draw a horse's head and body on cardstock. 2. Color it with realistic or magical patterns. 3. Cut out the shape and glue a lolly stick to the bottom. 4. Use the stick to gallop the horse across a table. 5. Create a "stable" out of a cardboard box for the puppet to sleep in.

title: split pin horse puppets
instructions: 1. Draw the horse's body, legs, and neck as separate pieces. 2. Use a hole punch or pin to create holes at the joints. 3. Connect the legs and neck to the body using split pins. 4. Ensure the pins are loose enough for the limbs to swing. 5. Move the legs to demonstrate different gaits like walking, trotting, or galloping.

title: moving eyes
what you'll need: Paper, markers, a straw or strip of paper
instructions: 1. Draw a face on a sheet of paper, but cut out two horizontal slits for the eyes. 2. On a separate strip of paper, draw two pupils. 3. Slide the strip through the slits behind the face. 4. Pull the strip back and forth. 5. Watch as the character's eyes "move" from side to side.

title: junk modelling instrument
what you'll need: Empty containers (tins, boxes), rubber bands, tape
instructions: 1. Collect various pieces of "junk" like a cereal box or a coffee tin. 2. Stretch rubber bands over the opening of the box to make a guitar. 3. Tap on the tins with spoons to make drums. 4. Tape two containers together to see how the sound changes. 5. Put on a "junk band" performance for an audience.

title: who's in the window
instructions: 1. Cut "window" squares out of a large piece of cardboard. 2. Draw different characters or animals on separate pieces of paper. 3. Tape the characters behind the windows. 4. Ask the child to "open" the windows to see who is living in the building. 5. Tell a story about how all the neighbors help each other.
variations: could be used for storytelling when something happens in a certain order e.g. gruffalo characters

title: tiny basketball toy
description: this is for children to play with, I am not expecting them to be able to fold it themselves.
instructions: 1. Fold a small piece of paper into a "hoop" and tape it to a wall or desk. 2. Crumple a small piece of paper into a ball (or use a ping pong ball). 3. Use your fingers to "flick" the ball toward the hoop. 4. Keep track of how many "baskets" you make. 5. Move further away to increase the difficulty level.

title: egg box whale
instructions: 1. Cut a single cup out of an egg carton for the body. 2. Paint the cup bright blue. 3. Cut a "tail" and "fins" out of blue paper and glue them to the back. 4. Poke a small hole in the top and insert a blue pipe cleaner for the "spout." 5. Draw a large smile and eyes on the front.

title: scissor skills
instructions: 1. Draw various lines on a sheet of paper (straight, wavy, zigzag). 2. Use a different colored marker for each line type. 3. Have the child use safety scissors to cut exactly along the lines. 4. Start with thick lines and progress to thinner ones. 5. Once cut, use the paper "strips" to make a collage.

title: transportation fingerprint art
instructions: 1. Use thumbprints to create shapes for vehicles (e.g., a long print for a bus). 2. Use markers to add wheels, windows, and tracks. 3. Create a "traffic jam" or a "busy harbor" scene. 4. Discuss the different ways we travel (land, sea, air). 5. Count how many wheels are in your picture.

title: paper sculpture techniques
description: make this with your child and then use the techniques in future projects
instructions: 1. Learn to "fringe" paper by cutting many small slits. 2. Create a "cylinder" by rolling and taping paper. 3. Fold an "accordion" to create springy movement. 4. Use "tabs" to glue 3D shapes onto a flat base. 5. Combine these techniques to build a complex paper city or sculpture.

title: egg box turtle
instructions: 1. Cut a single cup from an egg carton. 2. Paint it green to serve as the "shell." 3. Cut a flat "star" shape from green cardstock to serve as the legs and head. 4. Glue the egg cup shell onto the center of the cardstock. 5. Draw a face on the head and patterns on the shell.

title: my shadow art
what you'll need: Chalk or markers, sun or lamp, paper
instructions: 1. Place a piece of paper on the ground next to your own shadow. 2. Have a friend trace the outline of your shadow. 3. Try different poses, like "stretching" or "shrinking." 4. Fill the shadow outline with colors or patterns that represent you. 5. Discuss why the shadow changes length at different times of the day.

title: finger puppets
instructions: 1. Cut two small circles or "sleeves" that fit over your fingers. 2. Decorate them as characters (e.g., a king and a queen). 3. Draw faces and glue on small fabric scraps for clothes. 4. Use your fingers as "legs" to make the characters walk. 5. Put on a finger puppet play behind a "stage" made of a book.

title: cup launcher
what you'll need: Two paper cups, rubber bands, tape
instructions: 1. Cut the bottom out of one cup. 2. Hook a rubber band across the rim of the second cup using small notches. 3. Place the first cup over the second, stretching the rubber band. 4. Release! 5. The stored energy in the rubber band launches the cup into the air.

title: pre-scissor activities
instructions: 1. Place a variety of beans in a bowl. 2. Use tweezers to pick up one bean at a time. 3. Sort the beans into the different compartments of an egg carton. 4. This mimics the "pincer" movement needed for holding a pencil. 5. Try to do it faster each time to improve coordination.

title: paper chain jellyfish
instructions: 1. Make a standard paper chain out of colorful strips. 2. Cut a large "bell" shape out of paper for the jellyfish head. 3. Attach the paper chains to the bottom of the head as "tentacles." 4. Decorate the head with large eyes. 5. Hang it from the ceiling to watch it "swim" in the breeze.

title: elastic powered water bottle racecar
what you'll need: Plastic bottle, bottle caps (wheels), skewers, rubber band
instructions: 1. Build a chassis using a plastic bottle. 2. Use skewers and caps to create axles and wheels. 3. Loop a rubber band around the rear axle and secure the other end to the front. 4. Wind up the car by rolling it backward. 5. Release and watch the elastic force propel the car forward.

title: fly catch
instructions: 1. Decorate a paper cup. 2. Tie a string to a small paper "fly." 3. Attach the string to the cup. 4. Toss the fly and try to catch it in the cup. 5. This game improves focus and timing.

title: team cup grab
instructions: 1. Tie four long strings to a single rubber band. 2. Four people each hold one string and pull to stretch the rubber band. 3. Use the band to "grab" and lift a paper cup. 4. Move the cup to a new location and release it by slackening the strings. 5. This requires perfect communication and synchronized movement.

title: drop the spider
instructions: 1. Attach a paper spider to a long string. 2. Stand on a chair and try to "drop" the spider onto a target on the floor. 3. Adjust your aim based on where the spider lands. 4. Try dropping it while a fan is blowing to see how the "wind" affects it. 5. Discuss how spiders use their silk to drop safely.

title: pop up farm
instructions: 1. Fold cardstock in half. 2. Cut two slits in the fold and push the tab inward. 3. Glue a farm animal (cow, pig, sheep) to the tab. 4. When the card opens, the animal "pops up." 5. Use the card as a prompt to tell a story about life on the farm.

title: laser maze
what you'll need: Red yarn or string, hallway, tape
instructions: 1. Tape yarn across a hallway at different heights and angles. 2. The child must navigate through the "lasers" without touching them. 3. Crawl under, climb over, and step through the gaps. 4. If they touch a string, they have to start over. 5. Time the mission to see who is the stealthiest "spy."

title: peg grasshopper
instructions: 1. Color a wooden peg bright green. 2. Cut out long green paper hind legs and glue them to the back of the peg. 3. Add small paper eyes at the "mouth" end of the peg. 4. Clip the grasshopper onto a leaf or branch. 5. Squeeze the peg to make the grasshopper "bite" or hold onto things.

title: paper cup shark snacker
what you'll need: Paper cup, blue paint, string, paper "fish"
instructions: 1. Paint a paper cup blue and draw shark teeth around the rim. 2. Attach a string and a paper "fish" to the cup. 3. Flip the cup to catch the fish in the shark's mouth. 4. Discuss what sharks eat in the ocean. 5. See how many "snacks" you can catch in a row.

title: guess the object
instructions: 1. Place a secret object (spoon, toy car, sponge) inside a bag. 2. Have the child reach in and feel the object without looking. 3. They must describe the texture (hard, soft, bumpy) and guess what it is. 4. Reveal the object to see if they were right. 5. Switch roles and let the child hide an object for you.

title: wobblepeeps
instructions: 1. Cut a person shape with a rounded bottom. 2. Tape a penny to the inside of the bottom curve. 3. Place the "peep" on a flat surface and give it a nudge. 4. The weight of the penny makes the peep "wobble" but always return to an upright position. 5. Decorate with different expressions.

title: letter search
what you'll need: Tray, salt or sand, hidden letter cards
instructions: 1. Hide small cards with letters on them in a tray of salt. 2. Use a brush to "search" for the hidden letters. 3. When a letter is found, say its name and its sound. 4. Try to find all the letters in your name. 5. Discuss how archaeologists search for hidden history in the sand.

title: papercup carosal
instructions: 1. Decorate one cup as a carousel with horses. 2. Poke a hole in the bottom of both cups. 3. Connect them with a straw or skewer so the top cup can spin. 4. Blow on the "horses" to make the carousel turn. 5. Discuss how real carousels use motors to move in a circle.

title: dino balloons
instructions: 1. Blow up a balloon. 2. Tape cardstock dinosaur "feet," "spikes," and "heads" onto the balloon. 3. Use markers to draw scales on the rubber surface. 4. Discuss how air fills the balloon to give the dinosaur its shape. 5. Gently bat the "dino balloon" in the air to see how it floats.

title: paper snake
instructions: 1. Cut a long, wavy snake shape out of paper. 2. Draw colorful patterns or scales along the body. 3. Fold the paper into an accordion shape. 4. When you pull the head, the snake "stretches." 5. Discuss different types of snakes and their habitats.

title: egg box toadstools
what you'll need: Egg carton, red and white paint
instructions: 1. Cut individual cups out of an egg carton. 2. Paint the cups bright red. 3. Once dry, add white "polka dots" with a cotton swab. 4. Use these as "toadstools" in a mini garden. 5. Discuss which mushrooms are safe to touch in nature.

title: walk the plank
what you'll need: Long wooden plank or tape on the floor
instructions: 1. Place a plank on the ground (or use tape to mark a line). 2. Imagine you are on a pirate ship. 3. Walk from one end to the other without stepping off the "plank." 4. Try walking with a "treasure" balanced on your head. 5. Walk backward for an extra challenge.

title: DIY googly eyes
what you'll need: Clear plastic (from a toy box), markers, googly eyes
instructions: 1. Cut small circles out of clear plastic. 2. Place a black bead or draw a dot in the center. 3. Glue a slightly larger circle of cardstock behind it. 4. Shake to see the eyes wiggle. 5. Use these DIY eyes for all your future junk modeling projects.

title: binoculars
what you'll need: Two toilet paper rolls, tape, string
instructions: 1. Tape two cardboard tubes together side-by-side. 2. Attach a string to the sides so they can hang around your neck. 3. Go on a "nature spy" mission. 4. Use the binoculars to focus your vision on specific birds or leaves. 5. Discuss how focusing on one thing helps you notice more detail.
variations: just roll paper if you don't have tubes  or make a telescope

title: paper cup acrobat
instructions: 1. Decorate a paper cup as an acrobat. 2. Attach a string horizontally. 3. Balance the cup on the string. 4. Use pennies as weights on the "arms" to keep the acrobat from falling. 5. Discuss how the weights lower the center of gravity to provide stability.

title: papercraft hair
instructions: 1. Draw a face on a piece of paper. 2. Cut the top of the paper into thin, long "hairs." 3. Use a pencil to "curl" the hair by wrapping it around the barrel. 4. Give the character a "trim" using safety scissors. 5. This practices the rhythmic cutting motion needed for advanced art.

title: web shooters
description: this is for children to play with, I am not expecting them to be able to make it themselves.
instructions: 1. Build a "web shooter" using a paper cup attached to a wrist strap. 2. Use a spring or rubber band to launch a "web" (yarn or string). 3. Target practice by aiming at "villain" targets across the room. 4. Discuss how Spiderman's shooters are a mix of science and technology. 5. Practice the "web-slinging" motion.

title: mini plane
instructions: 1. Glue a lolly stick across the top of a clothespin. 2. Glue a second lolly stick across the bottom. 3. Add a small "tail" fin made of cardstock at the back. 4. This creates a sturdy biplane model. 5. Test how it "glides" when tossed gently onto a soft surface.

title: 2 ingredient putty
instructions: 1. Mix a small amount of toothpaste with cornstarch in a bowl. 2. Knead with your hands until it becomes a soft, pliable "putty." 3. Observe how it stretches when pulled slowly and breaks when pulled quickly. 4. Add a drop of food coloring for variety. 5. This is a great tactile tool for stress relief and focus.

title: jumping frog
instructions: 1. Fold a paper "frog" using origami techniques. 2. Press down on the back of the frog and slide your finger off. 3. The tension in the paper acts like a spring, launching the frog forward. 4. Race your frog against a friend's. 5. Discuss how real frogs use their powerful legs to jump.

title: communicative art
instructions: 1. One person starts a drawing with a single line or shape. 2. The next person adds one more element. 3. Continue taking turns to build a "communicative" masterpiece. 4. Do not plan the image beforehand; let it grow naturally. 5. Discuss what the final image looks like to each person.

title: texture book
what you'll need: Cardboard, various materials (sandpaper, silk, bubble wrap)
instructions: 1. Glue different materials onto the pages of a small book. 2. Close your eyes and turn the pages. 3. Describe the feeling of each page (rough, smooth, squishy). 4. Use the book as a "calm down" tool by focusing on the textures. 5. Discuss how we use our sense of touch to learn about the world.

title: nature busy book
instructions: 1. Go on a nature walk and collect "loose parts." 2. Tape or glue the items into a notebook. 3. Draw what you think the rest of the plant looked like. 4. Label the items by color or size. 5. This creates a living record of the seasons in your local area.

title: tin foil boats
instructions: 1. Give each child a piece of foil. 2. Design and build a boat that can float. 3. Add pennies to the boat one at a time. 4. Observe whose boat can hold the most weight before sinking. 5. Discuss how the shape of the boat affects how much water it displaces.

title: picking beads out of playdough
instructions: 1. Hide beads deep inside a ball of play dough. 2. Use your "pincer" fingers to dig through the dough and find the beads. 3. This strengthens the small muscles in the hand. 4. Sort the beads by color once they are "rescued." 5. This is a great pre-writing exercise.

title: Agamograph
instructions: 1. Draw a picture on a piece of paper. 2. Fold the paper like a fan (accordion style). 3. On one set of folds, draw a different picture. 4. When you look at the paper from the left, you see one image; from the right, you see another. 5. This "Agamograph" demonstrates how perspective changes what we see.

title: dino eggs
what you'll need: Balloon, flour (or play dough), toy dinosaur
instructions: 1. Place a tiny dinosaur inside a balloon. 2. Fill the balloon with flour or water and freeze/seal. 3. The "egg" must be "hatched" to find the dinosaur. 4. Discuss how dinosaurs laid eggs like birds. 5. Use the dinosaurs for imaginative play.

title: invisible ink
description: REMEMBER: TUMERIC STAINS VERY EASILY
instructions: 1. Mix baking soda and water to make "invisible ink." 2. Write a message on paper and let it dry. 3. Mix turmeric and rubbing alcohol (or water) and brush it over the paper. 4. The message will turn bright red! 5. **REMEMBER**: Turmeric stains everything it touches, so wear an apron.

title: construction lolly sticks
instructions: 1. Use lolly sticks to build 2D shapes (triangles, squares). 2. Stack the shapes to create 3D towers. 3. See who can build the tallest structure that doesn't fall. 4. Discuss how triangles provide more stability than squares in engineering. 5. Use the structures to house small toys.
variations: try different types of fasteners e.g. poppers, magnets

title: cardboard weaving frame
instructions: 1. Cut a "frame" out of cardboard and wrap it with yarn to create a grid. 2. Go outside and find long leaves, grasses, or twigs. 3. "Weave" the nature items through the yarn grid. 4. Observe the patterns and textures created by the natural materials. 5. This is a great way to display "nature treasures" from a walk.

title: spin drum
what you'll need: Cardboard circle, string, beads, lolly stick
instructions: 1. Glue a lolly stick to a cardboard circle. 2. Attach two strings with beads at the ends to the sides of the circle. 3. Twist the stick back and forth between your palms. 4. The beads will hit the cardboard, creating a rhythmic "drum" sound. 5. Decorate with bright patterns to match the music.

title: fruit printing
what you'll need: Apples, lemons, or oranges, paint, paper
instructions: 1. Cut a piece of fruit in half. 2. Dip the cut side into paint. 3. Press the fruit onto paper to create a print. 4. Observe the internal patterns (seeds, segments) of the fruit. 5. Use different fruits to create a colorful "fruit salad" artwork.

title: help holding scissors
instructions: 1. Place a sticker at the end of a line on a piece of paper. 2. Have the child "cut their way to the sticker." 3. This provides a clear goal and motivation for practicing scissor skills. 4. Use different types of paper (thick card vs. thin tissue) to vary the difficulty. 5. Discuss safety rules when using scissors.

title: lego marble maze
instructions: 1. Build a "maze" on a LEGO baseplate using bricks for walls. 2. Create a start and finish point. 3. Tilt the board to guide a marble through the path. 4. If the marble gets stuck, redesign the walls to make the path smoother. 5. Challenge a friend to solve your maze.

title: construction foam
instructions: 1. Mix shaving cream and glue to create "foam." 2. Use the foam to build 3D structures on cardstock. 3. Once dry, the foam remains "puffy" and soft. 4. Add food coloring to create colorful "buildings." 5. This is a great sensory-heavy construction project.

title: running rollers
instructions: 1. Tape cardboard tubes to a wall at different angles to create a "roller coaster." 2. Drop a marble in the top and watch it roll through the tubes. 3. Adjust the angles to make the marble go faster or slower. 4. See if you can make the marble land in a cup at the end. 5. Discuss how gravity pulls the marble down the track.

title: roots and shoots
what you'll need: Clear jar, wet paper towel, bean seeds
instructions: 1. Place a wet paper towel inside a glass jar. 2. Tuck a few bean seeds between the towel and the glass. 3. Place the jar in a sunny spot. 4. Observe over several days as the roots grow "down" and the shoots grow "up." 5. Discuss what plants need to survive (water, light, air).

title: pipe cleaner figures
instructions: 1. Bend pipe cleaners to create the "skeletons" of small people or animals. 2. Add pom-poms for heads and glue on googly eyes. 3. Use the figures to act out stories. 4. These "bendy" characters can sit, stand, or climb. 5. Create a whole family of pipe cleaner friends.

title: magic torch picture
description: If you want this to look good you'll want to use dark pens
what you'll need: Ziploc bag, black cardstock, flashlight cut-out
instructions: 1. Draw a scene on a Ziploc bag using permanent markers. 2. Place a piece of black cardstock inside the bag; the drawing will "disappear." 3. Create a "flashlight" out of white paper. 4. Slide the white flashlight between the black card and the bag. 5. The white paper "lights up" the drawing as you move it around.

title: lolly stick colour match dominos
instructions: 1. Paint the ends of lolly sticks in different colors (e.g., half red, half blue). 2. Take turns placing a stick down, but only if the color matches the end of the previous stick. 3. This is a simplified version of dominos. 4. See how long of a "train" you can build. 5. Discuss the strategy of saving certain colors for later.

title: cartwheelers
instructions: 1. Draw different "movements" on cards (hop, spin, clap). 2. When the music plays, children "cartwheel" or dance. 3. When the music stops, show a card. 4. Everyone must perform the action on the card. 5. This encourages listening skills and physical coordination.

title: paper cup mood indicator
instructions: 1. Draw different "faces" (happy, sad, angry) around the bottom of one cup. 2. Cut a window in a second cup. 3. Place the window cup over the face cup. 4. Rotate the cup to show how you are feeling today. 5. Use this as a tool to help children express their emotions without words.

title: egg box jellyfish
instructions: 1. Cut a single cup from an egg carton. 2. Paint it a "sea" color. 3. Attach long pieces of yarn to the bottom for tentacles. 4. Glue on googly eyes. 5. Hang the jellyfish from the ceiling and watch it "float."

title: paper dancers
instructions: 1. Draw a "dancer" silhouette on paper. 2. Use a straw or stick to make it a puppet. 3. Put on music and make the paper dancer move to the rhythm. 4. Encourage the child to copy the "dance moves" of the puppet. 5. Discuss how different types of music make us want to move in different ways.

title: 2 ingredient cloud dough
instructions: 1. Mix 1 part conditioner with 2 parts cornstarch. 2. Knead together until it feels like a soft, silky cloud. 3. This dough is extra soft and smells great. 4. Use it to "mold" clouds or snowballs. 5. Observe how the texture is different from traditional play dough.

title: bug search
instructions: 1. Go into the garden with a magnifying glass. 2. Look under rocks and leaves for "bugs." 3. Count how many different legs, wings, or colors you see. 4. Draw a picture of your favorite bug in a "nature journal." 5. Discuss why bugs are important for the environment.

title: bridge balance
instructions: 1. Place two lines of tape on the floor as a "bridge." 2. Scatter "treasures" along the bridge. 3. The child must walk the bridge and pick up the treasures without falling off. 4. Increase the difficulty by making the bridge narrower. 5. See how many treasures they can carry at once.

title: butterfly/dragonfly
description: for dragonfly wings try tracing around 2 fingers (do on folded paper so you only need to do it once)
instructions: 1. Fold a piece of paper in half. 2. Trace around two fingers to create the shape of a dragonfly wing. 3. Cut out the shape while folded to ensure symmetry. 4. Glue the wings to a lolly stick "body." 5. Decorate with bright "jewel" colors.

title: face prints
instructions: 1. Have the child look in a mirror. 2. Paint their face (with safe face paint!) and then "stamp" it onto paper. 3. Alternatively, paint a face on a large piece of paper and press another paper on top. 4. Observe the "print" of the face. 5. Discuss how our features make us who we are.

title: flapping butterfly
instructions: 1. Draw a butterfly on paper and cut it out. 2. Fold the wings slightly. 3. Blow air through a straw at the "body" of the butterfly. 4. The air pressure makes the wings "flap" up and down. 5. Discuss how wind helps insects and birds fly.

title: ride in caterpillar tracks
instructions: 1. Step into two large, open cardboard boxes. 2. Slide your feet forward like you are on "caterpillar tracks." 3. Race a friend across the room. 4. This build leg strength and coordination. 5. Discuss how heavy machines use tracks to move over soft ground.

title: quiet game
